newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up, property sector help hailed.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up, property sector help hailed.

text.p: Thai stocks rose for a second successive day on Monday as investors bought discounted, large capitalised stocks on optimism a new government plan to issue zero-coupon bonds would help the property sector, brokers said.

"Today's buying was a kind of follow through from Friday. Investors bought bank, finance and communication stocks as they hoped that the new zero-coupon bonds would assist the property sector," said the broker at a foreign brokerage house.
The SET composite index gained 11.87 points, or 1.72 percent, to close at 703.32 on 4.03 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 1.27 points to 52.09.

Rerngchai Marakanond, governor of Bank of Thailand, said over the weekend that the government would soon float up to 100 billion baht, seven-year zero-coupon bonds to raise funds needed for the property sector to weather a four-year slump.
"Investors cautiously bought as they waited for the government announcement to finally launch the funds. They believe that the plans are practical" the broker who asked not to be identified said.
Other brokers said investors hoped that the issue would be considered by the cabinet at its weekly meeting on Tuesday.
Brokers said many investors stayed on the sidelines on Monday as they thought the market still lacked solid, positive news to boost investment.
"These investors may enter the market after they get a clearer picture of the government funds to help the property sector," the broker said.
The banking sector gained most in terms of value, rising 2.09 percent, followed by the finance sector gaining 0.38 percent. These two sectors were hammered last week.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising five baht to 177. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
